unit.title: Clinical Office Practice and Patient Safety

sections.learningObjectives:
- Follow the manufacturer's instructions for use (IFU) for devices, supplies, and chemicals, including dilution, contact time, storage, and personal protective equipment.
- Follow the facility's written policies and procedures, using the current approved version and the correct documentation and reporting channels.
- Escalate questions, errors, equipment problems, and scope concerns to the supervisor or licensed staff rather than improvising a solution.
- Recognize unsafe improvisation and substitute behaviors, and choose to stop, ask, and report instead.
sections.eli10:
### Question 1

An IFU is like the rulebook that comes with a new game: it tells you exactly how to use it so nobody gets hurt and it works right.

### Question 2

The label on a product is like the recipe on a food box: that is where the person who made it tells you the right way to use it.

### Question 3

Before you use a new cleaning spray, you read the label the same way you read the directions before playing a new board game.

### Question 4

Contact time is like leaving soap on your hands long enough to scrub germs away: if you wipe it off too fast, it did not get the job done.

### Question 5

Wiping early is like taking a cake out of the oven after five minutes when the recipe says thirty: it is not done yet.

### Question 6

Mixing a cleaner is like making juice from concentrate: the directions tell you exactly how much water to add so it comes out right.

### Question 7

Mixing bleach with other cleaners is like mixing two paints you have never seen before: you might make something smelly and dangerous instead of useful.

### Question 8

An expired disinfectant is like flat soda: it looks the same but it has lost its power, so you should not count on it.

### Question 9

A single-use needle is like a plastic fork from a picnic: you use it one time and throw it away, you do not wash it to use again.

### Question 10

Reprocessing an instrument is like washing a fancy sweater: you follow the tag on that exact sweater, not whatever you did for your last shirt.

### Question 11

Running a sterilizer is like baking bread: you must use the right oven temperature and time or the loaf is not done in the middle.

### Question 12

If the oven will not get hot enough, you do not just serve the raw cake; you tell a grown-up the oven is broken.

### Question 13

If a ruler has a broken end, you do not keep measuring with it; you get a working ruler and tell someone the old one is broken.

### Question 14

Wearing the safety gear a label asks for is like wearing a helmet and knee pads before riding a bike: it protects you even for a short trip.

### Question 15

A missing guard is like a broken seatbelt: you do not drive the car until someone who knows how fixes it.

### Question 16

An SDS is like the instruction card for a science experiment: it tells you what could go wrong and what to do if it does.

### Question 17

SDS sheets are like the fire escape map on the wall: they have to be somewhere everyone can find them fast.

### Question 18

Danger and Warning are like a big red stop sign versus a yellow slow-down sign: they tell you how careful you need to be.

### Question 19

Labeling a spray bottle is like writing your name and grade on your school supplies: it keeps people from grabbing the wrong thing.

### Question 20

If soap gets in your eye, you rinse it right away and tell a grown-up; you do not rub it or pretend it did not happen.

### Question 21

A policy is like the class rules everyone agrees to follow so the whole group can work together safely and fairly.

### Question 22

If the class rule says wash hands before snack, you wash your hands even if your friend skips it.

### Question 23

You follow the newest edition of the rulebook, not the old copy from last year that may have different rules.

### Question 24

Policies are kept in a shared binder or on the shared computer, like the class rules posted on the wall where everyone can read them.

### Question 25

The exposure control plan is like the school's fire drill plan: it is written down so everyone knows how to stay safe and what to do in an emergency.

### Question 26

If you are not sure a job is one you are allowed to do, you ask the teacher before starting instead of guessing.

### Question 27

If the directions on a box do not make sense, you ask an adult for help instead of guessing and maybe breaking something.

### Question 28

If one grown-up says one thing and the rulebook says another, you ask for help sorting it out instead of just picking one.

### Question 29

If a friend asks you to fix their bike's brakes, you take them to someone who knows how, because getting it wrong is dangerous.

### Question 30

A frayed cord is like a toy with a broken plug: you unplug it and tell a grown-up instead of playing with it.

### Question 31

If you knock over a glass and it cracks, you tell an adult so it can be cleaned up safely, even if you feel embarrassed.

### Question 32

The chain of command is like who to tell in a classroom: first your teacher, then the principal if it still needs attention.

### Question 33

A recall is like a toy being called back because it broke for other kids; you stop using it and give it to a grown-up.

### Question 34

If the art class runs out of the special blue paint, you tell the teacher instead of using glue for paint.

### Question 35

Guessing the time is like taking cookies out of the oven whenever you feel like it: sometimes they will still be raw.

### Question 36

You wear your helmet every time you ride, even if a friend says a short ride does not need one.

### Question 37

The law is like the school rule that says wear closed shoes; the class rule might add that they must also be non-slip. You follow both.

### Question 38

You put a used needle in its special strong box right away, like putting a broken piece of glass in the trash can instead of leaving it on the floor.

### Question 39

You wash your hands before eating and after using the bathroom every time, not just once a day.

### Question 40

If you find a bottle with no label, you do not drink it or smell it to guess; you show it to a grown-up.

### Question 41

You do not drive a car you have never learned to drive; you ask someone who knows to teach you or help.

### Question 42

Safety features are like the chain on a swing: taking them off to go faster makes a crash more likely.

### Question 43

When helping someone build a model, you read the instructions together instead of making up steps.

### Question 44

Using the wipe the right way is like using a mop on the floor and a sponge on the counter, not swapping them.

### Question 45

For the right answer about a product, you check the label, like checking the recipe instead of asking your friend who never cooked it.

### Question 46

A blood spill is cleaned with the special gloves and cleaner, like using the right mop and gloves for a big, messy spill at home.

### Question 47

It is like following both the recipe and your family's kitchen rule about washing your hands: you do both, and together they make it safe.

### Question 48

If you forget a step in the class project, you tell the teacher so you can fix it together instead of pretending you did it.

### Question 49

Improvising is like making up new rules for a board game instead of reading them, which usually causes confusion or trouble.

### Question 50

You do not sign your friend's name on their homework; you tell the teacher the paper is missing a name.

### Question 51

Some foods must stay cold in the fridge or they go bad; a test chemical is the same and has its own temperature rule.

### Question 52

You keep your juice box away from the cleaning cabinet so you never take a sip of the wrong bottle.

### Question 53

You put a chemical in a proper, labeled container, not in an old soda bottle someone might drink from.

### Question 54

Gloves are like a napkin: you use a fresh one each time and throw the dirty one away.

### Question 55

If the directions say bake at 350 degrees, you do not turn it to 500 just because someone says the cookies will be faster.

### Question 56

If the new class rule says line up on the left, you line up on the left even if everyone used to line up on the right.

### Question 57

If two different answer keys are floating around, you ask the teacher which one is the real one before grading.

### Question 58

If someone on the playground looks like they might pass out, you go get the nurse right away instead of deciding it is fine.

### Question 59

If you almost trip on a loose rug, you tell someone so the rug gets fixed before somebody actually falls.

### Question 60

When you are not sure how to do something, you ask for help instead of just trying anything.

### Question 61

Hand sanitizer is for hands, just like dish soap is for dishes; you do not use it to wash the car.

### Question 62

Even if you are in a hurry, you still wash your hands before dinner; being busy does not make it okay to skip.

### Question 63

Before making lemonade, you check the can to see how much water to add instead of pouring until it looks right.

### Question 64

If the class runs out of paper cups, you tell the teacher to get more instead of reusing someone's used cup.

### Question 65

You write your homework in the right notebook right away, not on a scrap of paper you might lose.

### Question 66

You would not perform in the school play if you never learned the lines; you would say you need help from someone who knows the part.

### Question 67

Rules in the classroom exist so everyone stays safe and learns, not to make things harder or to show off.

### Question 68

When something spills in science class, you follow the teacher's clean-up plan with the right gloves instead of touching it with your hands.

### Question 69

If you cannot read the expiration date on milk, you ask a grown-up instead of drinking it and hoping it is fine.

### Question 70

If the thermometer says a very high number, you show it to the nurse instead of writing down a number you think is better.

### Question 71

You put your name on your test paper right away so it does not get mixed up with someone else's.

### Question 72

School rules change when a new law or a new problem comes up, like adding a rule after someone gets hurt on the playground.

### Question 73

You follow the instructions that match your exact model, like using the manual for the right video game console.

### Question 74

If two adults tell you two different ways to do a chore, you ask which one is right instead of mixing both.

### Question 75

If the grown-up who usually helps is gone, you still read the directions or ask another grown-up instead of making it up.
